description: The bar chart illustrates real-user demand in the Wildchat dataset by context-length range, showing separate counts for input demand versus output demand for four ranges (2K, 4K, 8K, 16K), with the caption noting that “2K” corresponds to the interval [2K, 4K) and similarly for the other ranges. The categorical axis is horizontal and presents four grouped positions in increasing order of range (2K, 4K, 8K, 16K), with each group containing two adjacent bars. The value axis is vertical, labeled “Number,” and uses a linear scale spanning from 0 to 120,000 with regularly spaced tick marks at 20,000-unit intervals. In each group, the left bar uses a solid fill to represent input demand and the right bar uses a diagonal slash hatch to represent output demand, as indicated by the legend along the bottom. For the 2K range, the solid pale-yellow input bar is labeled 9,320 and the hatched pale-yellow output bar is labeled 78,188. For the 4K range, the solid salmon input bar is labeled 3,784 and the hatched salmon output bar is labeled 108,494. For the 8K range, the solid light-blue input bar is labeled 1,401 and the hatched light-blue output bar is labeled 17,865. For the 16K range, the solid dark-blue/gray-blue input bar is labeled 832 and the hatched dark-blue/gray-blue output bar is labeled 4,247. All bars have black outlines and numeric value annotations placed above the bar tops, and there is no additional visual emphasis beyond the solid-versus-hatched encoding and color coding by range.
